title: A non-time-constructible dominating function
statement: There exists a function $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $n\le T(n)$ for every $n$, but $T$ is not time constructible. Here time constructibility means both that $T(n)\ge n$ and that some finite binary Turing machine, on every input of length $n$, outputs the binary expansion of $T(n)$ and halts within $c(T(n)+1)$ steps for some positive integer $c$.
